reason: The historical scores vary widely, and there are no paired controls, so they do not establish which kernel block limits performance or predict a gain. I rank the K-loop scheduling proposal first because it directly tests load/compute overlap while keeping the four ZA tiles and arithmetic operations. Address-generation proposals follow, but their likely benefit is limited to loop overhead and the two post-indexed-load proposals overlap. The register_reuse proposal ranks below these: each K step already reuses its loaded vectors across the four FMOPA operations, so the proposed two-step unroll does not clearly reduce loads and adds register pressure. Packing and traversal changes have broader address or timed-work risks; transpose and tail proposals affect the fallback rather than the fixed n=512 path.
